stops.note: 'servant, one sent around'; Caesar's Gallic War says Gaulish nobles surrounded themselves with ambacti, dependants and clients
through Medieval Latin ambactia 'service, mission'; Renaissance states such as Milan and Venice began keeping permanent resident ambassadors in the 1400s
came through Middle French ambassadeur; the Vienna Convention on Diplomatic Relations of 1961 now codifies ambassadors' immunity

current_meaning: a diplomat sent by a state as its official representative abroad
